64-bit to 64-bit function which applies the AES inverse sbox to each byte
 in a 64-bit word.

Turn a round number into a round constant for AES. Note that the
 AES64KS1I instruction is defined such that the r argument is always
 in the range 0x0..0xA. Values of rnum outside the range 0x0..0xA
 do not decode to the AES64KS1I instruction. The 0xA case is used
 specifically for the AES-256 KeySchedule, and this function is never
 called in that case.

function cap_access_checks(
  auth     : Capability,
  auth_idx : capreg_idx,
  addr     : xlenbits,
  stored   : option(Capability),
) -> option(ext_data_addr_error) = {
  let (is_store, stored_tag, stored_global) : (bool, bool, bool) = match stored {
    None()  => (false, false, true),
    Some(c) => (true, c.tag, cap_global(c)),
  };
  if not(auth.tag) then
    Some((CapEx_TagViolation, auth_idx))
  else if isCapSealed(auth) then
    Some((CapEx_SealViolation, auth_idx))
  else if not(is_store) & not(cap_permit_load(auth)) then
    Some((CapEx_PermitLoadViolation, auth_idx))
  else if is_store & not(cap_permit_store(auth)) then
    Some((CapEx_PermitStoreViolation, auth_idx))
  else if is_store & stored_tag & not(cap_store_cap(auth)) then
    Some((CapEx_PermitStoreCapViolation, auth_idx))
  else if is_store & stored_tag & not(stored_global) & not(cap_store_local_cap(auth)) then
    Some((CapEx_PermitStoreLocalCapViolation, auth_idx))
  else if not(inCapBounds(auth, addr, cap_size)) then
    Some((CapEx_LengthViolation, auth_idx))
  else
    None()
}

function cap_block_checks(auth : Capability, idx : capreg_idx, addr : xlenbits)
         -> option(ExecutionResult) = {
  let vaddr = Virtaddr(addr);
  let block = caps_per_block * cap_size;
  assert(plat_cache_block_size_exp == sizeof(log2_cap_block_size),
         "the tag group is the CBO block, so the two must be configured alike");

  if not(auth.tag) then
    Some(Ext_DataAddr_Check_Failure((CapEx_TagViolation, idx)))
  else if isCapSealed(auth) then
    Some(Ext_DataAddr_Check_Failure((CapEx_SealViolation, idx)))
  else if not(cap_permit_load(auth)) then
    Some(Ext_DataAddr_Check_Failure((CapEx_PermitLoadViolation, idx)))
  else if not(cap_load_cap(auth)) then
    Some(Ext_DataAddr_Check_Failure((CapEx_PermitLoadCapViolation, idx)))
  else if not(inCapBounds(auth, addr, block)) then
    Some(Ext_DataAddr_Check_Failure((CapEx_LengthViolation, idx)))
  else if not(is_aligned_addr(vaddr, block)) then
    Some(memory_exception(vaddr, E_Load_Addr_Align()))
  else
    None()
}

  & check_aperture_map()
  & check_vlen_elen()
  & check_vext_config()

  & check_extension_param_constraints()

privilege argument this carried is gone with the modes (R-15-003), and what

executing PCC *is* the privilege mechanism, so a compartment without it cannot
reach a CSR at all (R-15-003, R-15-073).

source.contents:
function generate_dts() -> string = {
  let clock_freq : nat = plat_clock_frequency;

  // `hex_str` is used for the unit-addresses of the `memory@` and `clint@` nodes
  // instead of `hex_bits_str` since they cannot have leading zeros.  These addresses
  // also cannot have a '0x' prefix which explains the `string_drop(., 2)`.

  "/dts-v1/;\n"
^ "\n"
^ "/ {\n"
^ "  #address-cells = <2>;\n"
^ "  #size-cells = <2>;\n"
^ "  compatible = \"ucbbar,spike-bare-dev\";\n"
^ "  model = \"ucbbar,spike-bare\";\n"
^ "  chosen {\n"
^ "    bootargs = \"console=hvc0 earlycon=sbi\";\n"
^ "  };\n"
^ "  cpus {\n"
^ "    #address-cells = <1>;\n"
^ "    #size-cells = <0>;\n"
^ "    timebase-frequency = <" ^ dec_str(clock_freq / plat_insns_per_tick) ^ ">;\n"
         // Before the `cpu` node rather than after it, because a devicetree
         // source puts every property of a node ahead of its subnodes and `dtc`
         // refuses the other order outright.
^ generate_dts_core_roster()
         // The node name and `reg` follow `mhartid` rather than being written
         // as zero. The identity is a composition constant fixed by the roster
         // (R-15-052b), so a tree hardwiring it would describe hart zero to a
         // machine that is some other hart. The label stays `CPU0` because it is
         // a DTS label rather than an identity and `&CPU0_intc` below names it.
^ "    CPU0: cpu@" ^ string_drop(hex_str(plat_hartid), 2) ^ " {\n"
^ "      device_type = \"cpu\";\n"
^ "      reg = <" ^ dec_str(plat_hartid) ^ ">;\n"
^ "      status = \"okay\";\n"
^ "      compatible = \"riscv\";\n"
^ "      riscv,isa-base = \"" ^ generate_isa_base() ^ "\";\n"
         // NOTE: The "riscv,isa" property is marked deprecated but is
         // probably still widely used.
^ "      riscv,isa = \"" ^ generate_isa_string(Canonical_Lowercase) ^ "\";\n"
^ "      riscv,isa-extensions = " ^ generate_isa_string(DeviceTree_ISA_Extensions) ^ ";\n"

      ^ ">"
      ^ generate_dts_roster_entries(rest, false)
  }

function.comment:
THIS`(code)` is the architectural permission set the codepoint names, as the
expanded bitmap. It is total: every one of the 32 codepoints names a set.

THIS`(want)` is the codepoint of the largest admitted permission set
contained in `want`, which is how a mask reaches a non-orthogonal field: the
result is a subset of the input, so `candperm` can only ever remove
authority whatever mask it is handed (R-15-007b, R-15-007h). Where two
admitted sets of equal size both fit, the lower codepoint wins; the order of
the table above is part of the freeze.

val.comment:
A common idiom in asl is to take two bits of an opcode and convert in into a variable like
```
let elsize = shl_int(8, UInt(size))
```
THIS ensures that in this case the typechecker knows that the end result will be a value in the set `{8, 16, 32, 64}`

Similarly, we define shifts of 32 and 1 (i.e., powers of two).

The most general shift operations also allow negative shifts which go in the opposite direction, for compatibility with ASL.

64-bit to 64-bit function which applies the AES forward sbox to each byte
 in a 64-bit word.

64-bit to 64-bit function which applies the AES inverse sbox to each byte
 in a 64-bit word.

Turn a round number into a round constant for AES. Note that the
 AES64KS1I instruction is defined such that the r argument is always
 in the range 0x0..0xA. Values of rnum outside the range 0x0..0xA
 do not decode to the AES64KS1I instruction. The 0xA case is used
 specifically for the AES-256 KeySchedule, and this function is never
 called in that case.
8-bit to 32-bit partial AES Mix Column - forwards.
8-bit to 32-bit partial AES Mix Column - inverse.
32-bit to 32-bit AES forward MixColumn.
32-bit to 32-bit AES inverse MixColumn.

Applies the forward MixColumns step of AES to a 128-bit vector
 representation of its state.

Applies the inverse MixColumns step of AES to a 128-bit vector
 representation of its state.
Easy function to perform a forward AES SBox operation on 1 byte.
Easy function to perform an inverse AES SBox operation on 1 byte.

128-bit to 128-bit implementation of the forward AES ShiftRows transform.
 Byte 0 of state is input column 0, bits  7..0.
 Byte 5 of state is input column 1, bits 15..8.

128-bit to 128-bit implementation of the inverse AES ShiftRows transform.
 Byte 0 of state is input column 0, bits  7..0.
 Byte 5 of state is input column 1, bits 15..8.

Applies the forward sub-bytes step of AES to a 128-bit vector
 representation of its state.

Applies the inverse sub-bytes step of AES to a 128-bit vector
 representation of its state.

THIS(csrno, access_type) decides whether an access to csrno is allowed. The
privilege argument this carried is gone with the modes (R-15-003), and what
replaced it is the capability: the access-system-registers permission on the
executing PCC *is* the privilege mechanism, so a compartment without it cannot
reach a CSR at all (R-15-003, R-15-073).

val.comment:
Called at the end of every step when PC is advanced to the next
 instruction. This includes taken branches. It is not called when
 the hart is waiting in WFI/WRS. The parameter is the new PC.

THIS`(code)` is the architectural permission set the codepoint names, as the
expanded bitmap. It is total: every one of the 32 codepoints names a set.

THIS`(want)` is the codepoint of the largest admitted permission set
contained in `want`, which is how a mask reaches a non-orthogonal field: the
result is a subset of the input, so `candperm` can only ever remove
authority whatever mask it is handed (R-15-007b, R-15-007h). Where two
admitted sets of equal size both fit, the lower codepoint wins; the order of
the table above is part of the freeze.

val.comment:
Called when control flow is redirected from just executing the next instruction.
 This includes:

  * Unconditional jumps (jal, jalr)
  * Traps
  * Returning from trap handlers (mret, sret)
  * Conditional branches that are taken (even if the target is the same instruction that
    would have been executed if they were not taken).

 The parameter is the new PC. pc_write_callback() will also be called after
 this with the same parameter.

val.comment:
Isla allows registers to be set on the command line via the
  `-R/--register` flag. This function sets those registers to the
  provided values. It is a no-op for non-Isla targets.

  This enables a startup flow that works something like:
  ```sail
  function main() {
    // registers can be set using -I/--initial here
    initialize_model(); // defined by the architecture
    sail_reset_registers(); // registers can be set using -R/--register here
    ...
  ```

  This allows us to set the values of registers that would otherwise
  be initialised to some sensible default by the `initialize_model`
  function (overwriting a value set by `-I` at the beginning of execution).

val.comment:
Isla supports *relaxed* semantics for system registers. This works
  as follows: Writes to these registers are not guaranteed to occur
  immediately. When a value is read from such a register, any previous
  written value can be read. Re-reading the register within the same
  instruction is guaranteed to return the same value ([sail_end_cycle]
  allows a different value to be subsequently read).

  This function removes all but the very last write, so subsequent
  reads must see only that value.

  This function is a no-op for non-Isla targets.

  // available_fields : 511 .. 448,
  integer_data_available: 448, // Followed by RVFI_DII_Execution_Packet_Ext_Integer if set
  memory_access_data_available: 449, // Followed by R VFI_DII_Execution_Packet_Ext_MemAccess if set
  floating_point_data_available: 450, // TODO: Followed by RVFI_DII_Execution_Packet_Ext_FP if set
  csr_read_write_data_available: 451, // TODO: Followed by RVFI_DII_Execution_Packet_Ext_CSR if set
  cheri_data_available: 452, // TODO: Followed by RVFI_DII_Execution_Packet_Ext_CHERI if set
  cheri_scr_read_write_data_available: 453, // TODO: Followed by RVFI_DII_Execution_Packet_Ext_CHERI_SCR if set
  trap_data_available: 454, // TODO: Followed by RVFI_DII_Execution_Packet_Ext_Trap if set
  unused_data_available_fields : 511 .. 455, // To be used for additional RVFI_DII_Execution_Packet_Ext_* structs

bitfield RVFI_DII_Execution_Packet_V1 : bits(704) = {
   rvfi_intr      : 703 .. 696, // [87] Trap handler:            Set for first instruction in trap handler.
   rvfi_halt      : 695 .. 688, // [86] Halt indicator:          Marks the last instruction retired
                                //                                      before halting execution.
   rvfi_trap      : 687 .. 680, // [85] Trap indicator:          Invalid decode, misaligned access or
                                //                                      jump command to misaligned address.
   rvfi_rd_addr   : 679 .. 672, // [84]      Write register address:  MUST be 0 if not used.
   rvfi_rs2_addr  : 671 .. 664, // [83]                          otherwise set as decoded.
   rvfi_rs1_addr  : 663 .. 656, // [82]      Read register addresses: Can be arbitrary when not used,
   rvfi_mem_wmask : 655 .. 648, // [81]      Write mask:              Indicates valid bytes written. 0 if unused.
   rvfi_mem_rmask : 647 .. 640, // [80]      Read mask:               Indicates valid bytes read. 0 if unused.
   rvfi_mem_wdata : 639 .. 576, // [72 - 79] Write data:              Data written to memory by this command.
   rvfi_mem_rdata : 575 .. 512, // [64 - 71] Read data:               Data read from mem_addr (i.e. before write)
   rvfi_mem_addr  : 511 .. 448, // [56 - 63] Memory access addr:      Points to byte address (aligned if define
                                //                                      is set). *Should* be straightforward.
                                //                                      0 if unused.
   rvfi_rd_wdata  : 447 .. 384, // [48 - 55] Write register value:    MUST be 0 if rd_ is 0.
   rvfi_rs2_data  : 383 .. 320, // [40 - 47]                          above. Must be 0 if register ID is 0.
   rvfi_rs1_data  : 319 .. 256, // [32 - 39] Read register values:    Values as read from registers named
   rvfi_insn      : 255 .. 192, // [24 - 31] Instruction word:        32-bit command value.
   rvfi_pc_wdata  : 191 .. 128, // [16 - 23] PC after instr:          Following PC - either PC + 4 or jump/trap target.
   rvfi_pc_rdata  : 127 ..  64, // [08 - 15] PC before instr:         PC for current instruction
   rvfi_order     :  63 ..   0, // [00 - 07] Instruction number:      INSTRET value after completion.
}
